questions: Should the t-test be paired (stats.ttest_rel) or independent (stats.ttest_ind)? The reference uses ttest_ind, but the prompt says 't-Test on these differences' which could imply a paired test on the differences themselves.
If N is larger than the number of rows in the DataFrame, should the function raise an error, use all rows, or cap N at the number of rows?
Are NaN or infinite values in the columns allowed? If present, should they be ignored, raise an error, or propagate?
Should the absolute differences be computed as |col1 - col2| or |col2 - col1|? The order matters for signed differences but not absolute.
If there are ties in absolute differences, the clarification says heapq.nlargest selects the first N encountered. Does 'first' refer to the original row order in the DataFrame?
Should the t-test assume equal variances (stats.ttest_ind default) or use Welch's t-test (equal_var=False)?
Is the p-value returned as a scalar float or a numpy float? The example prints a float, but scipy returns a numpy type.
Should the function handle duplicate indices in the DataFrame, and if so, does the selection of largest differences consider index values or positional order?
